previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and recent right toe amputation was admitted for lower abdominal and flank pain, urinary frequency, and nausea, found to be in mild diabetic ketoacidosis. She had elevated blood glucose and an anion gap metabolic acidosis, managed with IV fluids and insulin, with resolution of DKA. Abdominal pain was not clearly linked to infection or obstruction—renal ultrasound was normal, and urinalysis showed no signs of UTI. Pain was managed with acetaminophen and tramadol, and her home diabetes and gastroparesis medications were resumed. Her hemoglobin dropped from 10.5 to 7.5, likely due to hemodilution, with no active bleeding. Chronic leukocytosis persisted but was deemed reactive. She remained stable, with no signs of infection in the foot wound, and was discharged home on her prior regimen with outpatient follow-up for CBC monitoring and diabetes management.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  TOE(S), 2+ VIEW LEFT

INDICATION:  History: ___ with toe bleeding and pain// fracture

TECHNIQUE:  Three views of the left great toe

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

Lucency through the medial aspect of the first metatarsal head is likely
projectional rather than a fracture.  Likely chronic fracture deformity of
distal second metatarsal.  Mild degenerative change of the midfoot.  Mild
degenerative changes great toe MTP joint.  Mineralization is normal.  There
are no erosions.  Vascular calcifications are noted along the dorsal and
plantar aspects of the foot, and along the lateral aspect of the great toe.

IMPRESSION: 

Lucency through the medial aspect of the first metatarsal head is likely
projectional rather than a fracture.  Follow-up radiograph in ___ days could
be obtained for further evaluation if clinically warranted.  No definite acute
fracture identified.

Likely chronic fracture deformity through the neck of the second metatarsal. 
Chronic stress reaction could have similar appearance.  Clinical correlation.

Moderate soft tissue swelling of the great toe and second toe.

EXAMINATION:  ___ DUP EXTEXT BIL (MAP/DVT)

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with unexplained calf pain// calf pain; r/o DVT

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale, color, and spectral Doppler evaluation was performed
on the bilateral lower extremity veins.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

There is normal compressibility, flow, and augmentation of the bilateral
common femoral, femoral, and popliteal veins. Normal color flow and
compressibility are demonstrated in the tibial and peroneal veins.

There is normal respiratory variation in the common femoral veins bilaterally.

IMPRESSION: 

No evidence of deep venous thrombosis in the right or left lower extremity
veins.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman s/p L hallux partial amputation// post op eval

COMPARISON:  Prior exam is dated ___

FINDINGS: 

AP, lateral, oblique views of the left foot were provided post amputation of
the great toe through the level of the midshaft proximal phalanx.  An
overlying bandage is noted.  Otherwise, no change from prior.

IMPRESSION: 

Post amputation changes at the great toe.

EXAMINATION:  NON-INVASIVE PERIPHERAL ARTERIAL STUDY

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with DM2, s/p partial hallux amputation w
podiatry on L on ___, bleeding was less than expected in OR.// podiatry and
medicine would like to know if there is established evidence of PVD and
degree.she is experiencing some post op pain, so feel free to call floor to
ask how status of patient is before timing study

TECHNIQUE:  Doppler ultrasound and pulse volume recordings were obtained at
multiple levels in both lower extremities

COMPARISON:  ___

FINDINGS: 

On the right side, triphasic Doppler waveforms are seen in the common femoral,
posterior tibial, dorsalis pedis arteries.

On the left side, triphasic Doppler waveforms are seen in the common femoral,
popliteal, posterior tibial arteries.

The right ABI is 1.43 and the left ABI is 1.01.  Pulse volume recordings
demonstrate likely artifactually depressed waveform in the thighs bilaterally,
given normal waveforms in the right calf, mildly abnormal in the right ankle
and metatarsal level.  Pulse volume recordings on the left demonstrate normal
waveforms of the calf and ankle, severely abnormal in the left metatarsal.

IMPRESSION: 

No evidence of flow-limiting stenosis in either lower extremity.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  Normal left ABI with severely abnormal left metatarsal
pulse volume recording which can be consistent with arterial occlusive disease
of the foot.

Right ABI elevated and could be consistent with artifact secondary to arterial
calcification.

Compared to prior, pulse volume  recordings are now severely abnormal at the
left metatarsal level.

EXAMINATION:  US UPPER EXTREMITY, SOFT TISSUE

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with left axillary swollen tender lymph nodes
would like to assess for fluid collection// Axillary abscess?

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale ultrasound images were obtained of the superficial
tissues of the left axilla.

COMPARISON:  None

FINDINGS: 

Transverse and sagittal images were obtained of the superficial tissues of the
left axilla demonstrate a 1.2 x 0.7 x 1.2 cm hypoechoic lesion with a rim of
vascularity, possibly representing an infected sebaceous or epithelial
inclusion cyst.  There are 2 other tiny foci of hypoechogenicity in the
inferior layer of the dermis, likely representing sweat glands.


IMPRESSION: 

1.2 cm hypoechoic lesion in the left axilla with a rim of vascularity,
possibly representing an infected sebaceous or epithelial inclusion cyst. 
Please note that this lesion is too small to drain.
